notes.q: Lichtenstein's first work to feature the large-scale use of hard-edged figures and Ben-Day dots was Look Mickey (1961, National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.).

notes.name: Wikipedia · Roy Lichtenstein
notes.q: In 1961, Leo Castelli started displaying Lichtenstein's work at his gallery in New York.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Roy Lichtenstein
notes.q: Lichtenstein had his first one-man show at the Castelli gallery in 1962; the entire collection was bought by influential collectors before the show even opened.

src.name: Wikipedia · Roy Lichtenstein
src.q: In the late 1960s, they rented a house in Southampton, New York that Larry Rivers had bought around the corner from his own house.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Roy Lichtenstein
notes.q: It was purchased by the Tate Gallery in 1966, after being exhibited at the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1963, and (now at the Tate Modern) has remained in their collection ever since.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Roy Lichtenstein
notes.q: In 1964, Lichtenstein became the first American to exhibit at the Tate Gallery, London, on the occasion of the show "'54–'64: Painting and Sculpture of a Decade."

notes.name: Wikipedia · Roy Lichtenstein
notes.q: The title of a Life magazine article in 1964 asked, "Is He the Worst Artist in the U.S.?"

src.name: Wikipedia · Roy Lichtenstein
src.q: He moved back to New York to be at the center of the art scene and resigned from Rutgers University in 1964 to concentrate on his painting.
